title: Put the sample cuvette in the spectrophotometer: held only by its frosted sides, turned a quarter turn so its clear windows face the beam, lowered upright into the chamber's 16 mm well
instruction: Put the sample in the spectrophotometer.
context: Absorbance readings in a 1 cm cuvette are among the most common measurements in clinical, biology and chemistry labs, and the instrument manuals are explicit about the cell: "Handle cuvettes on the frosted sides only. Place the cuvette into the chamber so that the "reading" (clear) sides face left and right" (Molecular Devices SpectraMax user guide); "The light beam is directed from RIGHT to LEFT through the cell chamber as indicated by the arrows next to the chamber", with the "frosted side of cuvette facing you so the clear sides are aligned with the direction of the light beam", and "Wipe any fingerprints" (Valencia College technique sheet); the UBC wiki says the same. A cell put in the wrong way round sends the beam through its frosted sides, and a fingerprint or pad mark on a window scatters the light; either way the reading is wrong. Here the sample cuvette stands in a rack with its clear sides facing front and back, and the instrument's chamber well, marked with right-to-left beam arrows, needs them facing left and right. The instruction only says to put the sample in. The cuvette has to be picked up by its frosted sides, turned a quarter turn in the hand, kept upright (it is three-quarters full and open), and lowered into a well only 1.75 mm wider than it on each side, then let go. In the US alone, clinical laboratory technologists and technicians (343,000), biological technicians (74,400), chemical technicians (60,000) and chemists and materials scientists (93,500) held about 571,000 jobs in 2025 (BLS Occupational Outlook Handbook); loading samples into instruments is routine work for all of them and a core step for lab robots.
setup: Positions in cm on the table from the midpoint between the two arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left; heights above the table top. A UV-Vis spectrophotometer (a 20 x 24 cm body, 7 cm tall, 4 kg, loose) stands at x 34, y -2; its cuvette chamber is open: a 16 mm square well 1.5 cm deep (its top 5 mm opening to 22 mm) at x 28, y -10, its floor 5.5 cm up, with orange arrows either side showing the beam running right to left (along y). A standard 1 cm cuvette (12.5 mm square, 45 mm tall, 4.5 g with about 3 ml of pink sample, loose) stands in a shallow blue plastic cuvette tray (a 6 x 6 cm plate with one 32 mm square well 8 mm deep, 150 g, loose) at x 40, y -24. Two of the cuvette's sides are frosted white, the other two clear; in the rack the clear sides face front and back (along x).
scoring: Score 0 for the whole trial if at any moment a gripper is closed on the cuvette with its pads on the clear windows (its closing axis within 45 deg of the windows' normal), the cuvette tips more than 25 deg (an open, three-quarters-full cell spills), falls faster than 0.6 m/s (dropped) or ends on the table. Otherwise: 1.0 for the cuvette seated on the well's floor (within 2 mm) with its clear sides within 10 deg of facing the beam, let go (both grippers 3 cm or more away) and still; 0.5 for it in the well, so turned, but not seated or still held; 0.25 for it lifted out of the tray and held; 0 otherwise, including seated with the beam through its frosted sides. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0. On a real bench, the clear windows dusted with talc show any pad mark, and an overhead camera reads the cuvette's turn against the arrows and its tilt.
reset_notes: Wipe the cuvette's windows, re-dust them, and stand it back in the tray the same way round.
fidelity: The cuvette is one rigid box of the right size and mass; the sample is drawn only (no liquid), so spilling is judged by tilt past 25 deg. The chamber's centring spring is left out: the well is a fixed 16 mm square (1.75 mm play a side) with a 5 mm, 22 mm lead-in at its top. PhysX point contacts give a flat pad no grip against turning, so the cuvette's contacts get a 6 mm torsional-friction patch (without it the cuvette spun to its diagonal in the pads). The instrument is a loose 4 kg box with that well; no lid, optics or reading are simulated, so a wrong reading is judged from the cuvette's orientation and where it was gripped.
scores: Dream-1 run: TBD (not run in this campaign). Scripted demo in Isaac Sim (yam_scripted, 17 Nov 2026): 1.0, success at step 369 on two nodes (dev-01, dev-08); pads on the frosted sides (closing axis 86.5 deg from the windows' normal), turned a quarter turn, seated 0.5 deg from square to the beam and 1.7 mm off the well's centre, never tilted more than 2.1 deg, let go 4 mm above the floor. TASK_DEMO=naive (frosted grip, no turn, seated): 0.0, seated with the beam through the frosted sides. TASK_DEMO=unsafe (gripped by the clear windows, then turned): 0.0, the windows were held.
